result.title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs
result.summary: Networks that predict angles, gaze directions, and rotations do not output these quantities directly: they emit raw coordinates that a fixed decoder, such as normalization, maps to the final prediction. Attribution methods are usually applied to the raw coordinates, so they can credit inputs for changes the decoder discards, such as rescaling a vector when only its direction matters. The resulting explanation can highlight inputs that have no effect on the prediction. We instead attribute through the decoder differential, which for normalization decoders reduces to a scaled tangent projection. We characterize invariance to output rescaling, show that every fixed smooth scalar target on a sphere has points of zero tangential sensitivity, and show that an endpoint-projected variant of Integrated Gradients can still attribute to scale-only inputs, whereas direct angular Integrated Gradients cannot. On synthetic tasks with analytically known relevance, ambient attribution assigns up to 72% of its mass to an irrelevant region. On MPIIGaze validation data, tangent Grad-CAM produces 44% greater prediction displacement under 10% pixel deletion. On PASCAL3D+ with a 6D rotation decoder, the full differential improves mean deletion displacement by 14.1 degrees over the ambient coordinate sum and by 13.8 degrees over a decoder-invariant scalar. Results for a two-polarity tangent LayerCAM variant are mixed: it exceeds ambient-sum LayerCAM on circular regression but no difference is detected on quaternion pose. These results separate two failure sources, radial contamination and scalarization loss. The approach uses existing attribution methods with decoder-aware targets, although some variants also require changes to attribution aggregation. An invariant attribution can still miss inputs that drive the prediction, so invariance and deletion performance should each be checked.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出角度、视线与旋转等结构化输出由固定解码器（如归一化）从原始坐标映射而来，归因应透过解码器微分（对归一化即为缩放后的切空间投影）进行；据此构造切空间归因变体，并在合成任务、MPIIGaze 与 PASCAL3D+ 上以删除位移衡量效果，同时区分径向污染与标量化损失两类失效来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 「经解码器微分归因、区分解码丢弃的信息」这一线索可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态经解码器读出答案时的贡献分配与视觉证据筛选问题，但其对象是几何回归输出而非推理轨迹，迁移性需阅读正文判断。
